title: Tizita (ትዝታ)
logline: A grandchild far from home remembers how their grandmother's morning coffee ceremony gathered everyone around her, and realises the coffee was only ever an excuse to be together.
audience: Ethiopian diaspora grandchildren aged 18-35, watching on a phone in a vertical feed, often in a second language, who grew up with buna at home and now live far from their grandparents.
intent: At the end the viewer should feel the warm ache of tizita (nostalgic memory) and the small, concrete urge to call a grandparent today.
style_block: warm hand-painted gouache illustration, visible brush texture and soft paper grain, golden early-morning light, earthy palette of roasted-coffee brown, ochre, deep eucalyptus green and white cotton, gentle soft shadows, subject centred in the frame with generous headroom, calm and intimate mood, no text, no letters, no watermark
negative_prompt: text, letters, logo, watermark, extra fingers, deformed hands, photorealistic, harsh neon colours

characters.name: Emama (grandmother)

shots.beat: Establish the place and the ritual of every morning
shots.reason: An establishing wide shot tells the viewer where and when we are before we meet anyone, and the single smoking chimney points us to one house.
shots.image_prompt: dawn over a green Ethiopian highland town on a hillside, small houses with corrugated tin roofs among tall eucalyptus trees, mist in the valley, a thin line of smoke rising from one small house in the centre
shots.motion_prompt: mist drifts slowly through the valley, the smoke rises gently, the camera slowly pushes in toward the house

narration.am: በየማለዳው፣ የአያቴ ቤት በቡና ሽታ ይነቃ ነበር።

shots.subtitle_en: Every morning, my grandmother's house woke up to the smell of coffee.

shots.reason: Introduces Emama through what she does with care, so we love her before we see her face up close.
shots.image_prompt: inside a traditional Ethiopian highland home with ochre mud-plastered walls and a packed-earth floor, the grandmother kneels and scatters fresh green grass on the floor in front of a small wooden rekebot coffee table lined with small white handleless cups and a black clay jebena coffee pot
shots.motion_prompt: she slowly scatters a handful of grass, the camera stays fixed

narration.am: እማማ መጀመሪያ ሳሩን ትጎዘጉዛለች፤ ሲኒዎቹንም በረከቦቱ ላይ ታሰልፋለች።

shots.subtitle_en: First, Emama spreads the fresh grass and lines up the cups on the little table.

shots.reason: A close-up of hands and smoke carries the sensory memory (sound, smell, heat) that the whole film is about.
shots.image_prompt: extreme close-up of only an old woman's two hands and forearms stirring green coffee beans turning brown in a flat iron pan over glowing charcoal in a small clay stove, wisps of smoke, her face is outside the frame
shots.motion_prompt: the hands stir the beans slowly with a metal stick, smoke curls upward, the camera stays fixed

narration.am: አረንጓዴው ቡና በምጣዱ ላይ ሲቆላ፣ ጭሱ ጎረቤቱን ሁሉ ይጠራል።

shots.subtitle_en: As the green beans roast in the pan, the smoke calls the whole neighbourhood.

shots.reason: Emama looks toward the camera, toward us, so the viewer is placed in the seat of the grandchild being invited.
shots.image_prompt: inside a traditional Ethiopian highland home with ochre mud-plastered walls and a packed-earth floor, a single grandmother sitting on a low wooden stool holds a flat black iron roasting pan full of small dark-roasted coffee beans with white smoke rising, tilting it toward the viewer and smiles warmly, soft window light
shots.motion_prompt: she gently wafts the smoke toward the camera and smiles, the camera pushes in slightly

narration.am: ጭሱን ወደ እኛ እያራገበች፣ «ኑ፣ ቡና ጠጡ» ትለናለች።

shots.subtitle_en: Fanning the smoke toward us, she says: "Come, drink coffee."
shots.notes: Wan draft (seed 1004) morphed the roasting pan into a camera (E17), so Ken Burns on the keyframe. After the Habesha references the pan looked like bread rolls; the prompt now names roasted coffee beans and seed 2004 was promoted.

shots.reason: A short, quiet insert slows the pace and gives the music a moment on its own before the rounds begin.
shots.image_prompt: inside a traditional Ethiopian highland home with ochre mud-plastered walls and a packed-earth floor, a small clay incense burner on a floor strewn with fresh cut grass, frankincense smoking on glowing charcoal, soft morning light through the smoke
shots.motion_prompt: the incense smoke curls slowly upward, the camera stays fixed
shots.subtitle_en: The incense smoulders, and the house fills with peace.

shots.reason: The pour from height is the iconic image of the ceremony, and naming abol, tona and bereka gives diaspora viewers words they may have half-forgotten.
shots.image_prompt: close-up of a round-bellied black clay jebena coffee pot with a long narrow neck, tilted by an old woman's dark brown hand, a thin stream of dark coffee flowing out of its spout down into a row of tiny white cups without handles on a wooden tray, only the hand, the pot and the cups in frame
shots.motion_prompt: a steady thin stream of coffee pours into the cup, steam rises, the camera slowly tracks along the row of cups

narration.am: የመጀመሪያው ዙር አቦል፣ ሁለተኛው ቶና፣ ሦስተኛው በረካ።

shots.subtitle_en: The first round is abol, the second tona, the third bereka.

shots.reason: The wide shot of the gathering is the emotional payoff of the invitation: coffee turns into community.
shots.image_prompt: inside a traditional Ethiopian highland home with ochre mud-plastered walls and a packed-earth floor, the grandmother seated at the centre, Habesha neighbours and children with Ethiopian faces on low stools in a circle around her holding small coffee cups, laughing together, warm light
shots.motion_prompt: people laugh and lean toward each other, the camera slowly pulls back

narration.am: በእያንዳንዱ ዙር ወሬው ይረዝማል፤ ሳቁም ይበዛል።

shots.subtitle_en: With every round, the stories grow longer and the laughter louder.

shots.reason: The proverb is the theme of the film, so it gets the longest hold on Emama's face as she hands a cup to a child.
shots.image_prompt: inside a traditional Ethiopian highland home with ochre mud-plastered walls and a packed-earth floor, medium close-up of one grandmother, a single figure, smiling with kind eyes as she hands a small white coffee cup to a child's small hands at the edge of the frame
shots.motion_prompt: she slowly hands the cup forward and smiles, the camera stays fixed

narration.am: እማማ ሁሌም ትላለች፦ «ቡና ሰበብ ነው፤ ዋናው መገናኘት ነው።»

shots.subtitle_en: Emama always said: "Coffee is only an excuse. What matters is being together."

shots.reason: The cut to a cold, grey present day is the turn of the story; seeing the grandchild from behind lets any viewer step into that place.
shots.image_prompt: present day, one single young man seen from behind standing alone at a window of a small apartment in a cold grey foreign city, holding a small white coffee cup with steam rising, cool blue light outside and warm lamp light inside
shots.motion_prompt: steam rises from the cup, light snow falls outside the window, the camera stays fixed

narration.am: ዛሬ ከቤት ርቄ፣ ቡና ባፈላሁ ቁጥር ያ ጭስ ይታወሰኛል።

shots.subtitle_en: Today, far from home, every time I make coffee, I remember that smoke.

shots.beat: The empty seat, and the call to action
shots.reason: Returning to the opening room, now with one steaming cup waiting, closes the loop and turns the memory into an invitation to the viewer.
shots.image_prompt: inside a traditional Ethiopian highland home with ochre mud-plastered walls and a packed-earth floor, the small wooden rekebot table on a floor strewn with fresh cut grass, one small white coffee cup still steaming beside the black jebena, an empty low stool beside it, golden morning light
shots.motion_prompt: steam rises slowly from the single cup, the camera pushes in very slowly

narration.am: ትዝታ ማለት ይኼ ነው። ሦስተኛውን ዙር ሳትጠጡ አትሂዱ — ዛሬ ደውሉላቸው።

shots.subtitle_en: That is tizita. Don't leave before the third round. Call them today.

music.caption: traditional Ethiopian tizita instrumental, hageregna highland folk music, slow and tender melody on krar lyre with masenqo bowed fiddle and washint bamboo flute, tizita pentatonic mode, Ethiopian traditional song feel, nostalgic and longing, very soft kebero hand drum, sparse arrangement that leaves room for a narrator, warm, intimate, no vocals
music.choice_reason: Seed 22 chosen by the director after listening to the first three candidates (seeds 11, 22, 33). Test 2 asked for a more traditional tizita/hageregna sound, so the caption was rewritten and seeds 44, 55, 66 generated.

cues.does: enters softly with the dawn, a sparse plucked lyre motif
pads warm up and fill out as the rounds are poured and people gather
thins to a single bowed line for the distance of the present day
the opening lyre motif returns and resolves under the end card

lines: Made with AI: the images, motion, music and voice were generated.
The characters are fictional; the ceremony is real. Call your grandparents.
